claims.text: First: which sequence is it? T1-weighted: fat is bright and water or fluid is dark; best for normal anatomy
claims.quote: For example, fat appears bright (high signal intensity) on T1-weighted images and relatively dark (low signal intensity) on T2-weighted images; water and fluids appear relatively dark on T1-weighted images and bright on T2-weighted images. T1-weighted images optimally show normal soft-tissue anatomy and fat

claims.text: T2-weighted: fluid is bright; best for showing abnormalities such as tumors, inflammation and trauma
claims.quote: T2-weighted images optimally show fluid and abnormalities (eg, tumors, inflammation, trauma).

claims.text: Read T1 and T2 together: they give complementary information
claims.quote: In practice, T1- and T2-weighted images provide complementary information, so both are important for characterizing abnormalities.

claims.text: Why MRI for the brain and cord MRI is preferred over CT when detailed soft-tissue contrast is needed, such as intracranial or spinal cord abnormalities
claims.quote: MRI is preferred to CT when soft-tissue contrast resolution must be highly detailed (eg, to evaluate intracranial or spinal cord abnormalities

claims.text: Brain: white matter lesions MRI is the most sensitive imaging test for multiple sclerosis
claims.quote: MRI is the most sensitive imaging test for MS

claims.text: Gadolinium: enhancement separates actively inflamed plaques from older ones
claims.quote: Gadolinium contrast enhancement can distinguish actively inflamed from older plaques.

claims.text: Spine: the cord Sagittal T2: look for the cord being compressed (for example by herniated discs); cord edema shows as abnormally increased T2 signal inside the cord
claims.quote: Sagittal T2-weighted MRI shows spinal cord compression at the C4-5, C5-6, and C6-7 intervertebral levels secondary to multilevel posterior disc herniations (pink arrows). The intramedullary T2 signal is abnormally increased, representing spinal cord edema (yellow arrow).

claims.text: Suspected cord compression: MRI right away; if MRI is not available, CT myelography
claims.quote: MRI is done immediately if available. If MRI is unavailable, CT myelography is done
